topics.titleTr: AI ile Dijital Ürün Satışı: Pasif Gelir Rehberi
topics.titleEn: Selling Digital Products with AI: A Passive Income Guide
topics.angle: guide + build and sell digital products with AI, and where 'passive' income really breaks
topics.brief: Story-led: earning with digital products built using AI. Sections: what sells (templates, Notion systems, prompt packs, ebooks, mini-courses); validating demand before building; using AI to produce and package fast; pricing and platforms (Gumroad, Lemon Squeezy, Etsy); distribution via newsletter and social; the honest ceiling of 'passive'. Key claims to verify: digital products rank among top creator/newsletter revenue models; they are cheap to produce with AI; distribution, not creation, is the real bottleneck. Primary sources: a 2026 digital-products/creator-economy report; Gumroad creator data. End with a first-product launch checklist.

topics.titleTr: AI Sesli Asistan Kıyaslaması: GPT-Live, Gemini, Claude
topics.titleEn: AI Voice Assistants Compared: GPT-Live, Gemini, Claude
topics.angle: comparison + which of the three voice assistants fits driving, research, or careful work
topics.brief: Data-led comparison of the 2026 voice wave. Sections: full-duplex (GPT-Live can speak+listen at once, interrupt naturally), Gemini Live's camera/screen perception and playful persona, Claude voice mode's precision and mid-chat model switching (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku). Decision table by use case: hands-free driving/cooking, live translation, long-form writing, document analysis. Key claims to verify: GPT-Live replaced Advanced Voice Mode July 2026; Claude voice update late July lets users switch models mid-conversation; Gemini Live adds visual input. Sources: OpenAI GPT-Live post; TechCrunch Anthropic voice update. End with a picker.

topics.titleTr: ChatGPT, Claude ve Gemini'de Özel Talimatlar
topics.titleEn: Custom Instructions in ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini
topics.angle: how-to + write reusable system prompts that make each assistant answer the way you want
topics.brief: Field-notes how-to on the one setting most people skip. Sections: what custom instructions actually control (tone, format, defaults) vs a full persona; where each lives (ChatGPT custom instructions, Claude profile/project instructions, Gemini's 'saved info' and Gems); a copy-paste template with role, constraints, output format; pitfalls (overstuffing, contradictions, stale context). Key claims to verify: all three expose a persistent-instruction surface; Gemini offers an AI rewrite button. Sources: FindSkill custom instructions guide; each vendor's help docs. End with three ready templates.

topics.titleEn: AI Meeting Assistants Compared in 2026
topics.angle: comparison + pick a notetaker for accuracy, privacy, and CRM fit
topics.brief: Data-led roundup of AI notetakers (Otter, Fathom, Granola, Copilot, Gemini/Meet, ChatGPT). Sections: transcription accuracy and speaker labels; summary + action-item quality; privacy and bot-in-the-room vs on-device capture; integrations (CRM, Slack, calendar); pricing. Key claims to verify: AI meeting-assistant market growth (~$3.24B 2025 toward $7.33B 2035); Meet/Gemini and Copilot bundle notetaking into suites. Sources: a 2026 market report; vendor pages. End with a picker by team size and compliance needs.

topics.titleEn: 1M-Token Context: What Actually Changes?
topics.angle: deep-dive + what huge context windows really unlock for everyday users, and where they still fail
topics.brief: Question-driven explainer aimed at non-engineers. Sections: what a context window is in plain terms; what 1M tokens equals (whole books, codebases, long transcripts); real wins (analyze a full report, keep a long project going) vs myths ('it remembers forever'); lost-in-the-middle and cost/latency trade-offs; when RAG still beats stuffing everything in. Key claims to verify: Claude Opus 5 ships 1M-token context (July 2026 changelog); long-context recall degrades in the middle. Sources: Anthropic changelog; a long-context eval paper. End with practical do/don't.

topics.titleTr: AI Sohbetlerini Düzenle: Projects ve Gems
topics.titleEn: Organize Your AI Chats: Projects and Gems
topics.angle: how-to + stop losing context by structuring work in Claude Projects, ChatGPT Projects, and Gemini Gems
topics.brief: Field-notes how-to for people whose AI history is a mess. Sections: the difference between organizing by engagement (Claude/ChatGPT Projects = shared files + instructions for a client/campaign) vs by persona (Custom GPTs and Gems = a reusable assistant); when to spin up a Project vs a Gem; file/knowledge limits; the single-model lock-in caveat. Key claims to verify: Projects share files+instructions across chats; Gems and Custom GPTs are persona-shaped; each locks to one model family. Sources: LumiChats and Stackviv 2026 comparisons. End with a folder-structure template.

topics.titleTr: AI ile Inbox Zero: E-posta Triyajı
topics.titleEn: Inbox Zero with AI: Smarter Email Triage
topics.angle: how-to + build a repeatable AI-assisted triage routine without letting AI send dumb replies
topics.brief: Story-led walkthrough of a week taming an inbox with AI. Sections: triage rules (respond/defer/delegate/delete) and how Gemini in Gmail and ChatGPT can draft, summarize threads, and extract tasks; templates and snippets; guardrails so nothing auto-sends; measuring time saved. Key claims to verify: Gmail's Gemini side panel can summarize and draft in context; over-automation causes tone/accuracy misfires. Sources: Google Workspace Gemini docs; a productivity study on email load. End with a 20-minute daily routine.

topics.titleEn: Grow Retention with a Short-Video Series
topics.angle: guide + turn one-off clips into a returning series that compounds watch time
topics.brief: Story-led guide on building a repeatable short-video series. Sections: pick a consistent premise + format; a hook framework for the first 3 seconds; batching and scripting; a rotating structure viewers return for; reading retention curves to iterate. Key claims to verify: series with a consistent premise and clear reason to return outperform one-offs; brands post ~9.5x/day and lean on AI for volume; repurposed clips can beat native when optimized. Sources: Sprout Social 2026 trends; OpusClip creator report. End with a 4-week series plan.

topics.titleTr: Shorts mu Reels mi TikTok mu? 2026 Kararı
topics.titleEn: Shorts vs Reels vs TikTok: Where to Post
topics.angle: comparison + where a creator should post short video first in 2026 and why
topics.brief: Question-driven comparison of the three short-video homes. Sections: audience and discovery mechanics per platform; monetization (TikTok Shop, Reels bonuses, YouTube Shorts revenue share); watermark/cross-post penalties; native aspect-ratio and caption rules; which platform rewards which niche. Key claims to verify: cross-posting with visible watermarks tanks reach; 9:16 native gets priority placement; each platform has distinct payout models. Sources: QuickFrame 2026 video trends; platform creator docs. End with a where-to-start-first decision matrix.

topics.titleEn: 7 Mistakes That Kill Sound-Off Video
topics.angle: mistakes + fix the errors that lose viewers watching muted
topics.brief: Contrarian mistakes post: most video is watched muted, yet creators design for sound. Sections: relying on auto-captions instead of burned-in text; front-loading nothing in the first frame; tiny/low-contrast captions; no visual hook; ignoring safe zones behind UI; wall-of-text captions; no on-screen payoff. Key claims to verify: majority of social video is consumed sound-off; burned-in captions lift watch time; auto-caption accuracy varies by platform. Sources: QuickFrame/Sprout 2026 data. End with a pre-publish caption checklist.

topics.titleTr: AI ile Sosyal Medya Videosu Üretmek
topics.titleEn: Make Social Videos with AI: A Workflow
topics.angle: how-to + a script-to-publish pipeline using AI video and editing tools
topics.brief: Story-led how-to on an end-to-end AI video pipeline for creators. Sections: ideate and script with an assistant; generate B-roll/clips with Sora or Veo and edit in Google Vids (Omni) or a clip tool; auto-caption and reframe to 9:16; brand consistency and disclosure; batch and schedule. Key claims to verify: Google Vids added Gemini/Omni for higher-quality generation and text-based edits (July 2026); Sora and Veo lead generation. Sources: Google Vids July 2026 update; vendor pages. End with a reusable production checklist.

topics.titleEn: Build Community, Not Followers, in 2026
topics.angle: contrarian + why follower count is a vanity metric and what to grow instead
topics.brief: Contrarian take: 2026's winners aren't the highest-volume posters but the best community builders. Sections: why reach without belonging doesn't convert; signals that matter (saves, shares, DMs, repeat viewers); moving fans to owned channels (newsletter, Discord); rituals that create return behavior; measuring community health over follower vanity. Key claims to verify: the biggest gains come from audience understanding and genuine community, not raw output; engagement/retention signals beat follower totals. Sources: Sprout Social and National University 2026 trend reports. End with a community-metrics dashboard.

topics.titleEn: Email Deliverability: A Practical Checklist
topics.angle: checklist + keep campaigns out of spam with authentication and list hygiene
topics.brief: Field-notes checklist for inbox placement. Sections: authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC, BIMI); warming a domain/IP; list hygiene and sunset policies; engagement signals Gmail/Outlook weigh; content triggers that flag spam; monitoring bounce/complaint rates. Key claims to verify: Gmail/Yahoo bulk-sender rules require DMARC and easy unsubscribe; engagement-based filtering dominates placement. Sources: Google bulk sender guidelines; a 2026 deliverability report. End with a pre-send deliverability checklist and tools to test placement.

topics.titleTr: Google Ads mı Meta Ads mı? Küçük Bütçe
topics.titleEn: Google Ads vs Meta Ads on a Small Budget
topics.angle: comparison + where a small budget goes furthest by intent vs discovery
topics.brief: Data-led comparison for founders spending their own money. Sections: intent vs discovery (search capture vs feed interruption); realistic CPC/CPM and learning-phase minimums; creative demands (keywords vs thumb-stopping video); attribution and privacy signal loss; when to run both. Key claims to verify: Google captures existing demand while Meta creates it; algorithms need a minimum conversion volume to exit learning. Sources: platform ads help; a 2026 paid-media benchmark. End with a first-$1,000 allocation plan.

topics.titleTr: AI ile Pazarlama Otomasyonu: Zapier, Make
topics.titleEn: Marketing Automation with AI: Zapier & Make
topics.angle: how-to + wire AI into no-code automations without brittle spaghetti
topics.brief: Story-led how-to building AI-in-the-loop automations. Sections: pick high-value repetitive flows (lead enrichment, reply drafting, content repurposing, reporting); connect ChatGPT/Gemini via Zapier or Make; add human-approval gates; handle errors and rate limits; cost control. Key claims to verify: SMBs know they need AI but not where to start; Zapier/Make expose LLM steps; approval gates cut error risk. Sources: Improvado AI marketing trends; Zapier/Make AI docs. End with three copy-me automations.

topics.titleEn: Landing Page Mistakes That Kill Conversions
topics.angle: mistakes + the recurring errors that leak conversions and how to fix them
topics.brief: Contrarian mistakes post challenging 'more copy = more trust.' Sections: vague headlines that don't match the ad; too many CTAs; slow LCP and layout shift; hero that hides the offer; missing social proof; forms that ask too much; no mobile-first design. Key claims to verify: message match between ad and page lifts conversion; Core Web Vitals affect bounce and rankings; fewer form fields raise completion. Sources: a 2026 CRO benchmark; Google Core Web Vitals docs. End with a 10-point audit.

topics.titleEn: Micro-Influencer Marketing for Small Brands
topics.angle: guide + run creator partnerships that beat big-name reach on a small budget
topics.brief: Story-led guide to micro-influencer campaigns. Sections: why 1k–50k niche creators convert better than mega accounts; finding and vetting for real engagement (not bought); briefing without killing authenticity; deal structures (gifting, flat fee, affiliate); tracking with codes/UTMs; disclosure and FTC/local rules. Key claims to verify: smaller creators show higher engagement and trust; authentic creator-led content outperforms polished ads. Sources: a 2026 influencer-marketing report; platform partnership docs. End with an outreach template and a simple ROI sheet.

topics.titleEn: ChatGPT Health: Connecting Your Records
topics.angle: deep-dive + what ChatGPT Health does, what it can't, and the privacy trade-offs
topics.brief: Question-driven explainer of ChatGPT's new Health experience. Sections: what it connects (supported health records, Apple Health) and the dashboard/contextual Q&A; genuinely useful cases vs where it must not replace a clinician; data handling, consent, and what leaves your device; regional availability limits. Key claims to verify: ChatGPT Health launched for eligible U.S. users July 2026, connecting records and Apple Health data; it's an assistant, not a diagnostic tool. Sources: OpenAI Health announcement; help-center notes. End with a safe-use checklist.

topics.titleTr: Gemini for Home: Akıllı Hoparlörde AI
topics.titleEn: Gemini for Home: AI on Your Smart Speaker
topics.angle: guide + what changes when Gemini replaces Assistant on Nest and Home devices
topics.brief: Field-notes guide to Gemini arriving on home devices. Sections: what Gemini for Home adds over classic Assistant (conversational follow-ups, richer routines); the new ~15-minute conversational memory window; which devices got it (incl. first-gen Home Mini and Nest Hub); setup and privacy controls; current gaps. Key claims to verify: July 23, 2026 rollout expanded memory to 15 minutes and brought Gemini Live to older speakers. Sources: 9to5Google July 2026 report; Google Home release notes. End with a setup-and-privacy checklist.

topics.titleEn: Health Wearables 2026: Rings and Glucose
topics.angle: deep-dive + where wearable health tech actually got better in 2026 and what to trust
topics.brief: Data-led survey of 2026 health wearables beyond step counts. Sections: smart rings and discreet tracking; next-gen biometric sensors; the push toward non-invasive glucose monitoring; earbuds with health + live translation; accuracy caveats and FDA/CE clearance vs 'wellness' claims. Key claims to verify: non-invasive glucose monitoring is approaching mainstream but accuracy is contested; wearables are shifting from fitness to health-centered sensing. Sources: 2026 consumer-tech trend reports; regulatory clearance databases. End with a what-to-trust buyer's guide.

topics.titleTr: AI Kulaklık ve Canlı Çeviri: Abartı mı?
topics.titleEn: AI Earbuds and Live Translation: Hype?
topics.angle: deep-dive + how real-time translation earbuds work and where they break
topics.brief: Contrarian reality-check on live-translation earbuds. Sections: how the pipeline works (ASR to MT to TTS) and why latency and turn-taking still feel awkward; accuracy across languages and noisy rooms; which ecosystems (Pixel Buds, others) lead; privacy of always-listening mics; realistic travel/meeting use vs marketing demos. Key claims to verify: earbuds now ship real-time interpretation; end-to-end latency and dialect coverage limit real conversations. Sources: 2026 consumer-tech reports; vendor spec pages. End with an honest 'buy it if…' verdict.

topics.titleTr: Akıllı Ev 2026: Matter ve Cihaz Uyumu
topics.titleEn: Smart Home 2026: Matter and Interoperability
topics.angle: guide + build a cross-brand smart home that actually works together in 2026
topics.brief: Question-driven guide to a brand-agnostic smart home. Sections: what Matter and Thread solved and what they didn't; hubs and border routers; picking devices that truly interoperate; the pull toward on-device AI and offline control; migrating from a single-vendor lock-in. Key claims to verify: 2026 demand centers on seamless cross-brand integration; on-device/offline functionality is gaining favor; Matter coverage is still uneven by category. Sources: 2026 consumer-tech trend reports; Matter/CSA docs. End with a compatibility-first shopping checklist.

topics.titleEn: Finding and Validating a Micro-SaaS Idea
topics.angle: guide + find a narrow, painful problem and prove demand before you build
topics.brief: Data-led guide to sourcing and validating a micro-SaaS idea. Sections: where niches hide (communities, review complaints, workflow gaps); the single-purpose-tool advantage; validation before code (landing page, waitlist, pre-sales, concierge MVP); realistic MRR bands ($1k–$50k) and margins; the 12–18 month timeline honesty. Key claims to verify: users prefer one tool that works over bloated platforms; ~77% of solopreneurs profit in year one but revenue uplift is often modest. Sources: 2026 solopreneur/micro-SaaS reports. End with a 7-day validation sprint.

topics.titleEn: SaaS Pricing: The Mistakes Founders Make
topics.angle: deep-dive + pricing frameworks and the traps that leave money on the table
topics.brief: Contrarian deep-dive arguing most founders underprice and over-tier. Sections: cost-plus vs value-based pricing; picking a value metric that scales with usage; good/better/best design and anchoring; free trial vs freemium vs reverse trial; raising prices without churn; localizing for markets like Turkey. Key claims to verify: value-based pricing outperforms cost-plus; too many tiers reduce conversion; grandfathering eases increases. Sources: a 2026 SaaS pricing benchmark; Price Intelligently-style research. End with a pricing-page teardown checklist.

topics.titleEn: Selling AI Automation Services to Businesses
topics.angle: guide + package and sell AI automation to SMBs who don't know where to start
topics.brief: Story-led playbook for an AI automation service business. Sections: the gap (SMBs want AI but lack a starting point); productized offers (audit, then retainer) built on Zapier/Make + ChatGPT/Gemini; scoping and pricing outcomes not hours; delivery and handoff; avoiding brittle builds and scope creep. Key claims to verify: SMB demand for guided automation is high; retainers give solopreneurs more stable income than one-offs. Sources: 2026 solopreneur reports; automation vendor case studies. End with a first-offer and proposal template.

topics.titleTr: Bootstrap mı VC mi? 2026 İçin Doğru Seçim
topics.titleEn: Bootstrap or VC? Making the Call in 2026
topics.angle: comparison + choose a funding path that matches the business you actually want
topics.brief: Question-driven comparison of funding paths in the AI era. Sections: what VC optimizes for (winner-take-all, big outcomes) vs bootstrapping (control, margin, optionality); how cheap AI-built products change the math; the middle path (revenue-based finance, angels); signals your idea fits one path or the other; founder lifestyle trade-offs. Key claims to verify: AI tooling lets tiny teams reach revenue faster and cheaper; sub-$50k MRR niches stay below VC-competition thresholds. Sources: 2026 startup-funding commentary; solopreneur reports. End with a decision checklist.

topics.titleEn: First SaaS Metrics: MRR, Churn, and CAC
topics.angle: guide + the handful of numbers an early SaaS founder must track and act on
topics.brief: Field-notes guide to the metrics that matter before you have a data team. Sections: MRR/ARR and net vs gross revenue retention; logo vs revenue churn; CAC, payback period, and LTV/CAC; activation and the aha moment; leading vs lagging indicators and a simple weekly dashboard. Key claims to verify: net revenue retention predicts durable growth; churn compounds faster than founders expect; CAC payback under ~12 months signals health. Sources: a 2026 SaaS metrics benchmark; common operator definitions. End with a starter metrics sheet.

topics.titleEn: Are PWAs Still Worth It in 2026?
topics.angle: deep-dive + when a PWA beats a native app and where platform limits still bite
topics.brief: Question-driven deep-dive on PWAs in 2026. Sections: what modern PWAs can do (installability, offline via service workers, push, file/hardware APIs); where iOS/Safari still limits them; install-friction and discovery; PWA vs native vs Capacitor/Tauri wrappers; a decision framework by app type. Key claims to verify: service workers and Web App Manifest enable install+offline; iOS push and API support lag Android; app-store discovery still favors native. Sources: web.dev PWA docs; caniuse feature tables. End with a PWA-or-not checklist.

topics.titleEn: API Versioning Strategies That Scale
topics.angle: guide + version an API without breaking clients or drowning in branches
topics.brief: Field-notes guide to evolving APIs safely. Sections: URI vs header vs media-type versioning trade-offs; additive/backward-compatible change discipline; deprecation policy, sunset headers, and communication; consumer-driven contract tests; when to fork a v2 vs evolve v1; GraphQL/gRPC evolution differences. Key claims to verify: additive changes avoid breaking clients; Sunset/Deprecation headers standardize retirement; contract tests catch breakage early. Sources: RFC 8594 (Sunset header); Stripe/GitHub versioning practices. End with a deprecation runbook.

topics.titleEn: Database Backups and Disaster Recovery
topics.angle: checklist + design backups and recovery you have actually tested
topics.brief: Data-led checklist for backups that survive real incidents. Sections: RPO/RTO targets; logical vs physical backups and PITR (WAL/binlog); the 3-2-1 rule and offsite/immutable copies; encryption and access control; and the part everyone skips—restore drills and game days. Key claims to verify: untested backups fail when needed; PITR needs continuous WAL archiving; immutable/offsite copies defend against ransomware. Sources: PostgreSQL PITR docs; a cloud provider DR guide. End with a quarterly restore-drill checklist.
